html:
Timur, also called Tamerlane, was a Turco-Mongol warlord from Transoxiana who conquered an empire from Delhi to Anatolia between 1370 and his death in 1405. He was one of the most successful and most brutal conquerors in history.

He was born in the 1320s or 1330s into the Barlas, a Mongol tribe that had become Turkic in speech, in the Chagatai Khanate. An injury left him lame in the right leg; Tamerlane comes from Persian "Timur the Lame". By 1370 he controlled the western Chagatai lands. He was not a descendant of Genghis Khan, so he ruled through puppet khans and took the title amir, but he married into the family and saw himself as heir to the Mongol Empire.

His campaigns, nearly every year of his rule:

  • Iran and Iraq, many times; cities that resisted were destroyed and towers of skulls built.
  • The Golden Horde, whose capital he sacked in 1395.
  • India: he sacked Delhi in 1398.
  • Syria, taken from the Mamluks in 1400 to 1401.
  • The Ottomans: at the Battle of Ankara in 1402 he captured Sultan Bayezid I.

He died in 1405 while setting out to invade Ming China.

He brought craftsmen and scholars from conquered lands to make Samarkand a grand capital. He met the historian Ibn Khaldun outside Damascus. The Timurid Empire he founded broke up soon after his death, but his descendants made Samarkand and Herat centres of art and science, and one of them, Babur, founded the Mughal Empire.
sum: Timur, also called Tamerlane, was a Turco-Mongol warlord from Transoxiana who conquered an empire from Delhi to Anatolia between 1370 and his death in 1405. He was one of the most successful and most brutal conquerors in history.
